questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which of the following is the source of a.c.?
questions.explanation: A dynamo produces alternating current. So it is a source of a.c.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which scientist discovered the magnetic effect of electric current?
questions.explanation: Oersted discovered that electric current produces magnetism. So his name is linked with magnetic effect of current.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which is the direction of the magnetic field when current is flowing upwards through a conducting straight wire?
options: Opposite to the direction of electric current
Perpendicular to the direction of electric current
questions.explanation: For upward current, the magnetic field goes anticlockwise. This is shown by Maxwell's right-hand thumb rule.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which statement is true for an alternating current source?
options: Its current value is always constant
It always keeps lamp brightness constant
questions.explanation: Alternating current changes its direction again and again. So its direction does not remain fixed.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: On which principle is the working of a transformer based?
questions.explanation: Mutual induction means one coil affects another coil by changing magnetic flux. A transformer works by this principle.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which relation correctly represents the transformer formula?
options: Vp x Vs = Np x Ns
questions.explanation: In a transformer, voltage ratio depends on the turns ratio. So Vp/Vs = Np/Ns.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which current flows only in one direction according to the chapter?
questions.explanation: Direct current flows in one fixed direction. It does not change direction like a.c.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which current changes its magnitude and direction with time?
questions.explanation: Alternating current changes its direction and value with time. That is why it is called a.c.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which device is mentioned as a source of direct current?
questions.explanation: A dry cell gives direct current. So it is a source of d.c.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the frequency of a.c. in Nepal according to the exercise?
questions.explanation: In Nepal, a.c. frequency is 50 Hz. It means 50 cycles in one second.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What does 50 Hz a.c. mean?
options: Current changes direction 50 times in one second
questions.explanation: Frequency means number of cycles in one second. So 50 Hz means 50 changes in one second.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the magnetic effect of current?
options: Production of magnetic field around a current-carrying conductor
questions.explanation: Electric current produces a magnetic field around a wire. This is called magnetic effect of current.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What does Maxwell’s right-hand thumb rule help to find?
options: Direction of magnetic field around a straight current-carrying wire
questions.explanation: Maxwell's right-hand thumb rule shows magnetic field direction around a straight current-carrying wire.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is a solenoid?
options: A long coil of many turns of insulated wire
questions.explanation: A solenoid is a long coil with many turns of insulated wire. It looks like a spring.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What happens to a solenoid when current passes through it?
options: It turns into an insulator only
questions.explanation: When current flows through a solenoid, it produces a magnetic field. So it behaves like a magnet.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which material is commonly placed inside a solenoid to make an electromagnet stronger?
questions.explanation: Soft iron core makes an electromagnet stronger. So it is placed inside a solenoid.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is magnetic flux?
options: Total magnetic lines of force passing through a surface area
questions.explanation: Magnetic flux means total magnetic lines passing through a surface. More lines mean stronger flux.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the SI unit of magnetic flux mentioned in the chapter?
questions.explanation: Weber is the SI unit of magnetic flux. It is written as Wb.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Where is the magnetic flux strongest in the diagram of a bar magnet?
options: Far away from the magnet only
questions.explanation: Magnetic lines are closest near the poles. So the magnetic flux is strongest there.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is motor effect?
options: Chemical effect of acid on metal
Force experienced by a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field
questions.explanation: Motor effect means a current-carrying wire feels force in a magnetic field. This force can produce motion.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which rule is used to find the direction of force in motor effect?
questions.explanation: Fleming's left-hand rule is used for motor effect. It shows the direction of force.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which part of a simple electric motor rotates?
questions.explanation: The coil carries current inside the magnetic field. So the coil rotates in a simple motor.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is electromagnetic induction?
options: Storage of charge in a dry cell
Production of sound by a magnet
Production of current due to change in magnetic flux
Direct heating of a bulb filament
questions.explanation: Electromagnetic induction produces current when magnetic flux changes. No change in flux means no induced current.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Who discovered electromagnetic induction according to the chapter?
questions.explanation: Michael Faraday discovered electromagnetic induction. Oersted discovered magnetic effect of current.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the working principle of a dynamo or generator?
questions.explanation: A generator makes current by changing magnetic flux. This process is electromagnetic induction.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the function of a transformer?
options: To increase or decrease a.c. voltage
questions.explanation: A transformer changes a.c. voltage. It can increase or decrease the voltage.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which transformer has more turns in the secondary coil than the primary coil?
questions.explanation: A step-up transformer has more turns in the secondary coil. So it increases voltage.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which transformer is used in mobile chargers according to the exercise idea?
questions.explanation: Mobile chargers need low voltage. So they use a step-down transformer.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why does a compass needle deflect near a current-carrying circuit?
options: Because the current produces a magnetic field
questions.explanation: Current in a wire produces a magnetic field. This field moves the compass needle.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why is an electromagnet used in an electric bell?
options: It is always a permanent magnet
It can be magnetized and demagnetized by switching current on and off
questions.explanation: An electric bell needs attraction and release again and again. An electromagnet can do this by switching current on and off.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which change increases the strength of an electromagnet?
options: Increasing the number of turns of the solenoid
questions.explanation: More turns in a solenoid make the magnetic effect stronger. So the electromagnet becomes stronger.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why does a ceiling fan not rotate when connected directly to a solar panel circuit mentioned in the exercise?
options: Solar panel gives no energy at all
Solar panel gives direct current, while such fan needs a.c.
questions.explanation: A solar panel gives direct current. But that ceiling fan needs a.c., so it does not rotate properly.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: When a bar magnet is moved rapidly into a solenoid, what happens compared with slow movement?
questions.explanation: Fast movement changes magnetic flux quickly. So a greater induced current is produced.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What happens when a bar magnet is held stationary inside a solenoid?
questions.explanation: When the magnet is still, magnetic flux does not change. So no induced current is produced.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why does the bulb connected to a bicycle dynamo not glow steadily?
options: The dynamo always produces equal current
The bulb does not need current
The speed of the dynamo changes as the bicycle speed changes
questions.explanation: When bicycle speed changes, dynamo speed also changes. So the current and bulb brightness also change.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: How can the current produced by a dynamo be increased?
options: Keep the magnet stationary far away
questions.explanation: Rotating the coil faster changes magnetic flux faster. So more current is produced.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why is the core of a transformer laminated?
options: To reduce loss of energy in the core
questions.explanation: A laminated core reduces energy loss. So the transformer works more efficiently.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why are the numbers of primary and secondary turns different in a transformer?
options: To obtain a required change in voltage
To make both voltages always equal
To use it as a compass
questions.explanation: The turns ratio controls the voltage change. Different turns are used to get the needed voltage.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which rule is used to find the direction of induced current in a generator?
questions.explanation: Fleming's right-hand rule is used in generator effect. It shows the direction of induced current.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is shown by denser magnetic lines of force?
questions.explanation: Dense magnetic lines show a strong magnetic field. So denser lines mean stronger flux.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: In the transformer formula, what does Np represent?
options: Number of turns in the primary coil
questions.explanation: Np means number of turns in the primary coil. Ns means number of turns in the secondary coil.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: A transformer has 550 primary turns and is connected to 220 V to obtain 20 V. How many secondary turns are needed?
questions.explanation: Use Vs/Vp = Ns/Np. So Ns = 20 x 550 / 220 = 50.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: If a transformer has secondary turns 10 times the primary turns and primary voltage is 220 V, what is the secondary voltage?
questions.explanation: Voltage is proportional to number of turns. Ten times more turns gives 10 x 220 V = 2200 V.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What happens when the current direction is reversed in a solenoid?
questions.explanation: The magnetic field depends on current direction. If current direction reverses, magnetic poles also reverse.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which pair correctly matches an effect and a device?
questions.explanation: Motor effect is used in an electric motor. It changes electrical effect into motion.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: A student wants to make a simple motor. Which set is most suitable from the chapter?
options: Coil, magnet, dry cell, pins and conducting wire
KClO3 and hard glass tube only
questions.explanation: A simple motor needs a coil, magnet, dry cell, pins and conducting wire. These parts make the motor circuit and magnetic field.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which statement best distinguishes a motor from a generator?
options: A motor changes electrical energy into mechanical effect, while a generator produces electrical energy by induction
A generator never uses magnetic field
questions.explanation: A motor changes electrical energy into motion. A generator makes electrical energy by induction.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: A transformer cannot work properly with direct current because its principle needs what?
questions.explanation: A transformer needs changing magnetic flux. Direct current does not change continuously, so it cannot work properly.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What happens to the galvanometer needle when magnetic flux linked with a solenoid changes?
questions.explanation: Changing magnetic flux induces current in the solenoid. So the galvanometer needle deflects.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which pair correctly matches rule and use?
options: Maxwell right-hand grip rule - direction of magnetic field of solenoid
Fleming left-hand rule - direction of induced current in generator
Fleming right-hand rule - direction of force in motor
Hubble law - direction of magnetic field
questions.explanation: Maxwell right-hand grip rule shows magnetic field direction of a solenoid. The curled fingers show the field direction.
